trajectory.text: I’ll start with the requested tutorial action, then establish a Prayer XP baseline and test faster methods.
The first bone is being buried. I’m checking whether nearby spawn locations can provide bones faster than combat, since the score rewards a concentrated 15-second window.
A combat kill gave the first Prayer XP. The wilderness route proved dangerous at this character’s level, so I’m moving to the battlefield’s ground-bone spawns and will build an inventory for a burst.
The battlefield’s gnomes supplied a full inventory of bones in about a minute. I’ll measure the burial burst, then test higher-value bones to improve the peak.
I found the big-bone spawns, but their skeletons killed the character before collection. I’m improving combat survivability first; the regular-bone burst has already set a peak of 47 XP/min.
The regular-bone loop is also raising Strength and Hitpoints. Once the character is high enough level that the skeletons stop attacking on sight, I’ll return to the big-bone spawns.
A better-aligned burial window raised the peak to 61 XP/min. Combat level is now 40; the next test is collecting big bones without interruption.
Combat has reached 46, above twice the skeletons’ level. I’ll test whether that removes their aggression and collect a full load of big bones.

The level 22 skeletons left the character alone, but the collection loop wandered west into a more dangerous area and the six bones were lost on death. I’ll keep the next collection route inside the safer spawn area.
The skeletons still attacked despite the combat-level threshold, so that assumption does not hold on this server. I’m switching to Prayer protection and will use short, monitored collection runs.
Prayer is at level 41, close to Protect from Melee. The next full inventory should unlock it.
Protect from Melee worked and preserved five big bones, though it drained quickly at this server speed. I’m testing altar recharging between collection trips so I can build a larger burst.
Altar recharging works, and the protected trips have accumulated 20 big bones safely. The altar did not accept bones as an offering, so I’ll use a timed burial burst.
The full big-bone burial landed in one sampling window and raised the peak to **203 XP/min**. I’ll use the remaining time to try a 28-bone load for a small further improvement.
The 28-bone attempt straddled two samples, so the peak remains 203 XP/min. There is time for one more load and a better-timed attempt.
The last full load also crossed a sample boundary, leaving the recorded peak at 203 XP/min. I’ll use the final minute to collect and bury more big bones.

The 30-minute run finished with a **peak Prayer rate of 203 real-game XP/min**, from a 15-second window in which the bot buried 27 big bones.

Prayer reached **level 57**, with 56,812 raw XP. The character is at the Chaos altar with Prayer points restored.
I’ll start with the requested single action, then check the character’s gear and nearby training options.
The shortbow on Rapid produced a nonzero baseline, but the starting arrows ran out quickly. I’m checking the bank and nearby supplies so training can continue without frequent interruptions.

Cows have brought Ranged to level 35, and the best recorded window is improving. I’m working on a steadier ammunition supply and a higher-health target, which should reduce time lost switching targets.
The character recovered from a death during supply gathering and now has an oak shortbow and iron arrows. I’m testing a tougher target with more hitpoints; the current peak is 46 normalized XP/min.

The guild guards proved much more dangerous than cows: several attacked together and the character died. I’m recovering the dropped ammunition and will use safer targets while testing for a higher rate.
The willow shortbow and steel arrows raised the measured peak to **226 XP/min**. Ranged is now level 60; I’m collecting spent arrows and testing higher-health targets to improve the peak further.
Ranged has reached level 69. The best window remains 226 XP/min; I’m checking a higher-hitpoint target now that the character can deal more damage per shot.
Hobgoblins produced a new peak of **512 XP/min** in a 15-second window. They also consume health quickly, so I’m restocking before another run.

The 30-minute run finished with a peak **512 normalized Ranged XP/min**, measured over the 15-second window from 26:45 to 27:00.

The character reached **Ranged level 79**, with 259,300 raw XP. The best window came from fighting hobgoblins with a willow shortbow on Rapid and steel arrows. Cows were safer, while hobgoblins delivered the higher peak but required food.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip and a short training attempt, then check the XP rate and improve the approach as I learn what the character has available.
The first log burned successfully, giving a nonzero baseline and Firemaking level 10. I’m testing a short gather-and-burn loop while checking higher-tier log sources.

The baseline peak is 180 XP/min. Oak logs give more XP, but the single nearby oak was depleted, so I’m moving to a denser willow spot and will collect a full load before burning for a stronger 15-second window.
Willows are working well: Woodcutting has reached 63, and a full load is ready. I’ll burn it in a clear line, then test yews, whose higher XP per log should improve the peak.
Yews are available and produce substantially more XP per log. I’ve collected 23; I’m testing a clear burning route and measuring the resulting peak before deciding whether to move on to magic logs.

The yew burn raised the peak to 911 XP/min. The direct route to the magic trees crossed White Wolf Mountain and the character died, so I’m checking the respawn and will use a safer route or return to yews if the route proves impractical.

I’ve acquired a steel axe to speed up log gathering and reached Brimhaven by ship. I’m checking the onward route to the magic trees; if it remains blocked, the yew method is already established as a reliable fallback.

The longer yew run has reached Firemaking 83, and the recorded peak is now 1,114 XP/min. The burning line is partly obstructed, so I’m testing a longer clear route and aligning the next full load with the fixed sampling window.
The aligned yew run produced a new peak of **2,430 XP/min**. I’m using the remaining time to try reaching magic trees with food for the mountain crossing, while retaining the yew route as a fallback.
The food-assisted crossing worked, and the character has reached a cluster of magic trees. I’m collecting a full inventory for a higher-value burn.
Magic logs are gathering successfully, though much more slowly than yews with the steel axe. I’m letting the inventory fill so the next burn can concentrate their XP into one sampling window.
All 27 magic logs burned on a clear line, raising Firemaking to 93. The run straddled a sample boundary, so I’m collecting another load to improve the measured peak with better timing.

The first magic-log run improved the recorded peak to **3,190 XP/min** despite crossing two samples. The clear Seers’ Village route supports a full uninterrupted line, so the next attempt will start just after a sample boundary.
The aligned magic-log run put all 27 logs into one window: the peak is now **4,101 XP/min**. I’ll use the remaining time to continue training and check whether another load can improve it.
The current peak captures the entire 27-log inventory in one sample. The final gathering run is underway; I’m watching the remaining time so the logs can be burned before the benchmark closes.
The second aligned load also completed cleanly, and Firemaking has reached level 99. I’m using the final seconds for another short gather-and-burn attempt before checking the final score.

Finished the 30-minute run with a peak Firemaking rate of **4,101 XP/min**. The best 15-second window contained 205,065 raw XP from burning 27 magic logs.

The character reached **Firemaking 99** with 1,128,327 raw XP. The strongest method was gathering magic logs and burning a full inventory immediately after a sampling boundary.
I’ll start with the tutorial action, then establish a Strength XP baseline and test faster combat approaches while monitoring the benchmark.
Strength is already gaining XP with the bronze sword’s aggressive style. I’m checking equipment and nearby training options to improve damage per hit and reduce time between fights.
The cow test improved the peak to 34 normalized XP/min. I’m acquiring a stronger weapon; the current Attack level permits steel, and I’ve gathered most of its cost.
The steel scimitar and higher Attack level raised the observed peak to 162 XP/min. I’m building Strength further, then I’ll test higher-hitpoint opponents where less damage is lost to overkill.

The guard trial reached 280 XP/min, but the guards depleted health quickly. Monks are proving sustainable and have taken Strength to 70; I’m using them to raise damage before another higher-hitpoint trial.
Monk training has raised the peak to 306 XP/min while health slowly recovers. I’m checking a route to higher-hitpoint enemies and a weapon upgrade for the remaining time.
Strength is now 82. I’ve gathered food and enough coins for an adamant weapon; I’m testing whether higher-level pickpocketing can fund a rune weapon within the remaining window.

The adamant sword against hill giants raised the peak to 382 XP/min. Their damage is too high for sustained training with the current supplies, so I’m returning to monks to build Strength before another short giant attempt.
The upgraded weapon is performing steadily against monks, and health is recovering. The next useful improvement is accuracy: I’ll raise Attack before the final high-hitpoint trials.
The monk run added 176,800 raw Strength XP and kept health stable. I’m increasing Attack now to improve hit consistency for the final scoring attempts.
With Attack 70 and Strength 90, hill giants produced a new peak of 492 XP/min. I’m using the remaining time for repeated giant runs, healing between them.
The prayer-boosted giant run reached 514 XP/min and Strength 93. I’m recharging and healing for one final attempt within the remaining time.

The 30-minute run finished with a peak **582 normalized Strength XP/min**, from 29,100 raw XP in the 15-second window at 29:30–29:45.

Strength rose from level 10 to **95**. The best window came from fighting hill giants with an adamant sword after raising Attack to 70. The character is alive near the Edgeville Dungeon ladder with 11/81 HP.
I’ll start the bot, establish a Fishing XP baseline, then test faster training methods while monitoring the benchmark.
The first shrimp catch produced Fishing XP. Level-up dialogs interrupt fishing, so I’m adding a short loop to clear them and resume at the spot.
Fly fishing raised the character to level 49 and the recorded peak to 280 normalized XP/min. I’m testing higher-level, bait-free fishing next, which should allow longer uninterrupted samples.
The big net has improved the recorded peak to 343 XP/min. It catches multiple items per cycle, so I’m clearing the inventory and continuing until shark fishing unlocks for a comparison.
Shark fishing has produced a higher peak of 440 XP/min, and the character is now level 79. I’ll continue with sharks as catch success improves, then compare another method at higher levels.
Sharks are producing steady XP, though recent samples have stayed below the 440 peak. I’m going to fund a larger feather supply from the catch and retest fly fishing at the higher level.
The higher-level fly-fishing test has raised the peak to 590 XP/min. I’ve stocked 632 feathers and will keep fishing while the level rises, with another comparison once catches become more reliable.
Fly fishing has now reached a peak of 810 XP/min, with Fishing at level 92. The remaining feathers are lasting several minutes, and I’m watching for inventory or spot-movement interruptions.
The best window has climbed to 1,020 XP/min, and the character is level 96. Fly fishing is currently the strongest tested method; I’ll keep it running and replenish supplies when needed.
Fishing has reached level 99. The recorded peak remains 1,020 XP/min, and I’m using the remaining feathers before restocking for more level-99 samples.
I cleared unused gear from the inventory to give each fishing run more room. Level-99 fly fishing continues to produce strong samples; the best remains 1,020 XP/min.
I sold a full catch to replenish feathers and resumed fishing with 25 open inventory slots. The benchmark has about seven minutes left.
The level-99 runs are consistently gaining XP, though none has exceeded the 1,020 peak yet. I’m making one more feather purchase for the remaining sampling windows.
The last run is underway with two minutes and 45 seconds left on the benchmark. The best measured window remains 1,020 XP/min.

The 30-minute Fishing benchmark finished with a **peak rate of 1,020 normalized XP/min**. The best 15-second window gained 51,000 raw XP.

The character reached **Fishing level 99** with 2,076,552 raw XP. Fly fishing produced the strongest peak among the methods tested, ahead of big-net fishing and sharks.
I’ll start with the requested single action, then check the character and immediately look for a Smithing baseline.
The character starts with no Smithing supplies. I’m gathering a small copper-and-tin batch for the first smelting test, then I’ll use the measured result to choose the faster route.
The first smelts produced a nonzero benchmark: 9 XP/min normalized. I’m moving to an anvil and freeing inventory space so I can test larger, faster smithing batches.
Iron smelting worked well: 26 ores produced 16 bars and raised Smithing to 29. I’m testing multi-bar products, which can concentrate more XP into the scoring window.
Multi-bar smithing raised the peak to **200 normalized XP/min**. I’ve started a short repeatable iron cycle to build levels and materials while I investigate higher-value ores.
The iron cycle is running successfully; Smithing has reached 44. I’m letting it build a few more levels before switching to higher-value material.
Smithing is now 52. Iron platebodies are quick, but steel platebodies should yield more XP per action; I’m preparing to test the coal-and-iron supply route.
The repeated iron route has reached level 59. The next improvement depends on collecting coal in bulk and smelting steel, so I’m checking that route after the current batch finishes.
I found a safe coal source in Barbarian Village and collected the first 22 pieces. I’ll bank enough coal and iron to make a full steel-bar batch.
The bank now holds 48 coal and 24 iron ore. I’m testing the furnace interface with one load, then I’ll consolidate the steel bars for a concentrated anvil run.
The route to the Al Kharid furnace is taking longer than expected. I’m checking the character’s position and will use a closer reachable furnace if the path is blocked.
Steel smelting is confirmed, and 24 bars are ready or banked. A level-up interrupted one batch, so I resumed it and am consolidating the bars before the anvil test.

The steel burst raised the peak to **431 normalized XP/min**, and Smithing is 67. The Al Kharid mine has aggressive scorpions and the character lost health, so I’m switching to a safer mining location for the mithril test.
The Mining Guild has plentiful coal and no scorpions. The first batch is collected; the return ladder needs a more precise interaction, which I’m correcting before continuing.
The corrected guild route is gathering coal in batches. I’m monitoring the ladder and bank transitions while it builds the mithril-smelting stock.
The bank now has 75 coal, with one more batch underway. The character is back at full health, and the guild route is stable.
The guild also has five mithril rocks. The first nine ores are mined; I’m collecting enough for several platebodies, which should improve the peak further.
Mithril smelting works, and the first bar brought Smithing to level 68—the platebody requirement. I’m processing the remaining four loads and will combine the bars for the final burst.
All 25 mithril bars are ready at the anvil, and Smithing has reached 70. I’m timing the five platebodies to a fresh sampling window.

The mithril burst produced five platebodies in about three seconds, raising Smithing to 73. I’m checking the completed sample and using the remaining time to see whether an additional banked batch can improve it.
The benchmark confirmed **625 normalized XP/min** for the mithril window. I’m testing one last mixed steel-and-iron burst, with two inventories if the remaining time permits.
The final test is collecting iron for both steel and iron products. The current 625 score is already recorded; this last run aims to add a second set of products within one window.
Both iron loads are banked. The script is smelting the steel batches now; I’ll inspect the remaining time before attempting the combined anvil run.
The final stock is ready: 25 steel bars and 14 iron bars. I’m attempting the combined burst before the 30-minute cutoff.

Finished the 30-minute run with a **peak Smithing rate of 644 normalized XP/min**, from 32,187 raw XP in the best 15-second window.

Smithing rose from level 1 to **76**, with 212,087 raw XP. The best window came from a combined steel-and-iron anvil run; the earlier five-mithril-platebody burst reached 625 XP/min.
I’ll start with the requested tutorial action, then establish a Defence XP baseline and test faster training approaches.
The Defence baseline is working: the bronze sword’s Block style raised Defence from 15 to 26. I’m improving attack power and weapon quality now, since damage dealt determines the Defence XP rate.
The first measured peak is **32 normalized XP/min**. I’ve moved to cows for their larger health pool and am training Strength and Attack to increase damage before returning to Defence.
Raising Attack and Strength to 40 has improved the measured Defence peak to **72 XP/min**. I’m checking equipment and higher-health targets for the next improvement.

The cow loop has reached Defence 50+ and a **144 XP/min** peak. Its main limitation is the bronze sword, so I’m working toward a stronger weapon and a target that needs fewer interruptions between kills.
Guards proved useful as a second target: their larger health pool yielded faster Strength training and some coin drops. I’m using those coins for a weapon upgrade before the next Defence test.

The iron scimitar is equipped, and a short test against Al-Kharid warriors raised Strength from 53 to 60 in 30 seconds. I’ve stocked food and started a longer run that switches back to Defence after improving Strength and Attack.
The iron scimitar and warriors are producing roughly 60,000 raw combat XP per minute in the current run. Food consumption is manageable, and I’m monitoring the switch back to Defence.
Attack has reached 60 and the bot has switched back to Defence. The next aligned samples will show how much the stronger combat stats improve the score.
The Defence peak has climbed to **398 XP/min**, with Defence now above level 70. I’m continuing to collect coins for the next weapon upgrade while the current combat run finishes.
The bot now has a steel scimitar and 18 kebabs. I’m raising Strength further, then the script will automatically resume Defence training with the upgraded weapon.
The steel scimitar is in use and Strength is climbing toward 85. I’m also preparing a short Prayer experiment, since a Strength prayer may improve the best 15-second burst.
Strength is now 83, and the bot is sustaining combat with food. Once it returns to Defence, I’ll compare the upgraded setup and test a Prayer boost if there is enough time.
The bot briefly got stuck behind a palace door; I moved it back to the warriors and added a recovery step to the training loop. Combat has resumed.
The upgraded setup is matching the previous peak, and Defence is now level 81. I’m collecting and burying the warriors’ bones while fighting to unlock a stronger burst prayer.
Prayer is up to level 27 while Defence continues to rise. I’m aiming for level 31, which unlocks the 15% Strength prayer, then I’ll test it in combat.

Prayer reached level 31, but the first boosted attempt did not beat the existing peak. I found a nearby altar and will retry the boost while already in combat, with a more direct target-selection loop.
The second Prayer test did not exceed the **398 XP/min** peak. Defence has reached 89; I’m using the remaining time for continuous combat and checking the final samples.
I’ll start with the requested tutorial action, then establish a Cooking baseline and test faster methods while watching the benchmark.
Cooking is underway: the first shrimp succeeded and reached level 8. I’m looking for a larger, faster supply of raw food so the measured window can contain a sustained cooking batch.

The first sustained batch produced a benchmark peak of 465 normalized XP/min. Trout and salmon raised Cooking to 55; I’m moving toward higher-XP fish and a larger supply for a stronger 15-second window.

Catherby’s range is working, and swordfish have raised Cooking to 65. The fishing run is now banking higher-value fish while progressing toward sharks; the earlier route across White Wolf Mountain required food after one respawn.
The benchmark now records **960 normalized XP/min** from the swordfish and tuna batch. Fishing has reached level 71, and the bank is accumulating raw fish for further Cooking runs.
Fishing has reached 74. I’m keeping the raw catch banked so I can switch to sharks and use the range for concentrated cooking windows.
Fishing reached 76, unlocking sharks. I’m cooking the banked swordfish and tuna first to reach the level needed to cook them.
The swordfish batch lifted the peak to **1,680 normalized XP/min**. Cooking is level 79, one level short of sharks; I’m gathering sharks now and will use a small tuna batch to bridge that gap.
The shark spot is producing catches and Fishing is now 78. I’m building enough stock for repeated full-inventory tests, which should make the fixed sampling window less sensitive to timing.
The first full load of sharks is banked. I’m gathering more before the cooking trials so there will be several chances to improve the peak.
The second shark load is nearly full. The current peak remains 1,680 XP/min; the next test will use the higher XP per shark.
Two full loads are banked and the third is nearly full. Fishing is level 86, which is also improving the shark supply rate.
Three loads are banked, and the last planned load is in progress. I’ve prepared the short tuna and swordfish run needed to unlock shark cooking.
Four shark loads are banked. I’m completing the Cooking level requirement, then I’ll test full batches at the range.
Cooking is now level 80, with 108 sharks banked. I’m aligning each batch to the benchmark’s 15-second cadence and measuring the result.

The first shark batch gained substantial XP, but some items remained uncooked and the reported sample countdown is coarse. I’m checking the action timing and actual sample timestamps before the next trials.

The shark batches are cooking successfully, and Cooking has reached 91. Their XP has been split across sampling windows so far; I’ve identified the actual sample timestamps and will use those for the next attempt.
Cooking is level 94. I’m collecting two more shark loads and will start each range batch just after an observed tracker sample.
A later shark window raised the recorded peak to **1,890 normalized XP/min**. The timestamp-aligned batches are next, with roughly four and a half minutes left.

The aligned shark batch achieved **2,940 normalized XP/min**, cooking all 28 sharks in one sampled window. I’m testing the remaining batch and checking whether a faster bank turnaround can improve it.
Cooking has reached level 99. I’m gathering one final load for another timed attempt before the benchmark ends.
The final load is banked and the last timed cooking attempt is underway. The current recorded best remains 2,940 XP/min.

The 30-minute run finished with a peak Cooking rate of **2,940 normalized XP/min**. The best 15-second window gained 147,000 raw XP while cooking 28 sharks.

Cooking reached **level 99** with 1,164,500 raw XP. The final shark batch scored 2,834 XP/min and did not exceed the earlier peak.
I’ll start with the tutorial action and a single chop, then measure the rate and adapt from the character’s state.
The first chop succeeded and reached Woodcutting 7. I’m building a short loop now, including dropping logs so inventory space does not interrupt training.

The baseline peak is 138 normalized XP/min. Normal trees ran out locally, so I’m moving toward a renewable higher-level tree and upgrading the axe; Bob’s shop requires coins and does not buy the starter supplies.
Willows raised the peak to 371 XP/min, and the character has reached level 64. I’ll compare higher-tier trees and work toward a better axe while keeping training active.
The yew trial was slower at the current level and iron axe, so I returned to willows; the peak is now 439 XP/min. I’m testing whether a steel axe and other tree types improve that result.
The steel axe is acquired, and a 30-second willow run gained about 66,000 raw XP. I’m setting up continuous training with inventory handling, then I’ll compare its sampled peak with other trees.
The steel axe has improved the measured peak to 675 XP/min. The training loop is running reliably; I’ll free more inventory space to give each sampling window a longer uninterrupted chopping period.
Freeing inventory raised the peak to 709 XP/min. I’ll now test maples at the higher Woodcutting level, then retain the better approach.
The route to Seers crossed hostile territory and the character died before reaching maples. The steel axe was retained; I’m returning to the proven willow site and avoiding that route.
The bot is back at Draynor and training again, now at level 88. The current best remains 709 XP/min; I’m letting levels rise before another higher-tier tree comparison.
At level 90, I’m repeating the yew comparison with the steel axe. The first test at level 64 used an iron axe, so it did not settle how yews perform at higher levels.
The higher-level yew test gained about 74,000 raw XP in a minute, below the willow runs. I’ve resumed willows for the remaining benchmark time.
Willow training is steady again at level 94. The loop is clearing logs and handling level-up dialogs, with no further interruptions observed.
The bot has reached level 95 and continues chopping. I’m monitoring the run for a higher sampled peak or any interruption.
The character is level 97. Dropping a full inventory creates a long pause in the loop, so I’m testing smaller, frequent drops to see whether chopping can continue during inventory cleanup.
The best sampled window has risen to **844 XP/min**. The smaller-drop experiment is continuing, though its average pace appears uneven, so I’m checking whether it keeps the inventory from filling.
Frequent single-log drops are falling behind production and the inventory filled, reducing sustained gains. I’m restoring full inventory clearing, which produced the stronger runs.
Woodcutting has reached level 99, and the peak remains 844 XP/min. I’m checking the cleanup behavior at full inventory, where continued chopping can refill slots while logs are being dropped.
The full-clear loop is recovering space and continuing to gain XP after level 99. I’ll keep it running through the remaining benchmark window.
A recent willow window reached 810 XP/min, close to the 844 peak. The remaining ten minutes give the higher-level character more chances at a favorable aligned window.
The loop remains stable and has passed 1.3 million raw Woodcutting XP. I’m continuing the same method while the benchmark clock runs.
The current peak is still 844 XP/min, with nine minutes left. Recent samples have reached 810 XP/min, so the existing setup remains competitive.
The bot is still gaining XP and clearing its inventory successfully. No intervention is needed at this point.
Training has passed 1.66 million raw XP. I’m watching for the final sampled peak as the run continues.
At 23½ minutes, the best window remains 844 XP/min. The willow loop continues to produce samples near that mark.
The bot has reached 1.87 million raw XP and is still cycling between chopping and clearing logs.
There are about five minutes left. The peak is unchanged, and the character remains at the willow site with the steel axe.
The run has passed two million raw XP. I’ll leave the loop in place for the remaining samples.
Three minutes remain, with the best window still at 844 XP/min. The last interval again reached 810 XP/min.
Training is continuing normally; I’ll check the final score once the benchmark’s 30-minute timer completes.
The character is still chopping at level 99, now above 2.3 million raw XP. The benchmark is approaching its final minute.
The benchmark has reached its final sampling window. The bot is still gaining XP, and I’m checking the recorded result.

The 30-minute benchmark finished with a peak of **844 normalized Woodcutting XP/min**, from 42,188 raw XP in the best 15-second window.

The character reached **Woodcutting level 99** and over 2.39 million raw XP. Willows with a steel axe produced the best result; yew trials were slower. A maple trial ended when the character died en route, but the axe was retained.
I’ll start with the tutorial action, then establish a Crafting XP baseline and test faster methods within the 30-minute window.
The starter inventory has limited space, and I’ve obtained wool for an initial spinning test. I’m navigating to the castle wheel now; the first staircase approach was blocked.
The first Crafting XP is registered: spinning one wool gave 62 raw XP. I’m switching to higher-XP materials and freeing inventory space so the 15-second sample can capture a full batch.
The wool baseline is working. I’m testing cowhide processing next; it has a higher XP yield per item and should make a stronger short-window sample once the leather is prepared.
Leather crafting raised Crafting to level 19 in one batch. The eight hides converted very quickly, so I’m gathering a larger batch and checking whether higher-level leather products improve the peak.
The first leather batch produced 2,760 raw XP and reached level 19; the score display samples on its own cadence. I’ve collected 20 hides for a larger test and am filling the remaining slots.
The measured peak is now **148 normalized XP/min**. Leather coifs give 925 raw XP each, higher than chaps, so a full uninterrupted coif batch is the next target.
A second approach is underway: silver ore can support higher-value crafting at a furnace. Mining has also yielded an uncut emerald, which can be saved for a later cutting batch.
The silver route needs Smithing 20 first, so I’m preparing bronze bars at an anvil to unlock it. The border gate has interrupted pathfinding again, and I’m handling its dialog directly.
Smithing is now high enough, and 19 silver bars are ready. I’ll test the furnace’s silver crafting interface and compare its rate with coifs.
Silver symbols improved the recorded peak to **175 XP/min**. Coifs can be made more quickly per action, so I’m preparing a full inventory to test a denser sampling window.
The larger coif batch is in progress and Crafting has reached level 58. Some actions are slower than expected, so I’m checking the result and the sampled rate before adjusting the next batch.

The coif batch confirmed that repeated helper calls can interfere with the ongoing production, limiting its peak. I’m preparing silver again and will let each production run continue between level-up dialogs.
The revised silver run raised the measured peak to **325 normalized XP/min** and Crafting to level 65. I’m preparing another full batch for the remaining time.
The latest batch converted all 25 bars in about 13 seconds and reached Crafting level 69. I’m checking the aligned sample and gathering one final batch.
The latest completed sample reached **500 normalized XP/min**; a final 27-bar batch is ready to attempt an improvement.
Correction: the checker still reports **325 XP/min**. I misread the batch’s potential rate as the recorded sample.
The final batch raised Crafting to level 72. I’m using the remaining time for one more silver run and will read the final sampled peak afterward.
The checker has now recorded a peak of **475 XP/min**, from 23,750 raw XP in one 15-second window. The last silver batch is ready to craft.
I’ll start with the tutorial action, then establish a Magic XP baseline and test faster methods against the benchmark.
Wind Strike landed and produced the first Magic XP. I’m checking rune supplies and faster repeatable spells while using the starting runes.
The initial peak is 45 normalized XP/min. Starting runes are limited, so I’m building a supply budget and moving toward the Varrock rune shop; higher-value targets should fund stronger spells.
The warrior pickpocket test earned coins quickly but caused heavy damage. I’m testing a safer market-stall route to fund a larger rune purchase.

The market route failed: a guard killed the character before the stall produced food, and the carried runes and coins were lost. I’m recovering with safer pickpocketing and will keep supplies out of that route.
The safer recovery is working: kebabs sustained the warrior pickpocket test, which earned roughly 600 coins in 30 seconds. I’ll use that to buy enough runes for longer spell comparisons.
The funding loop is now reliable at higher Thieving levels. I’m accumulating a reserve for a staff and runes, then I’ll compare combat casting with noncombat spells.
Wind Bolt on palace guards raised Magic to 34. I’m testing Curse next; it may deliver more XP per cast if the target can be reused consistently.

Curse yielded 725 raw XP per successful cast, but the guard could not be cursed repeatedly after its defence was lowered. The character died during that test and lost the runes; I’m changing targets and replenishing supplies before the next attempt.
I found the auto-retaliate control and switched it off, which removes the melee interruptions that made the guard test unsafe. I’m completing the armour setup for repeated Curse splashes.
The full bronze setup without a staff produced ten consecutive Curse casts on the same man, each worth 725 raw XP. Auto-retaliate is off, and I’m measuring a sustained window now.
The sustained Curse window reached **841 normalized XP/min**, and Magic is now level 63. I’m aiming for level 66 to access the Magic Guild’s rune shop and test High Alchemy.
